name: Błażej Dubiel
title: Software Engineer
summary: Software engineer with 4+ years of experience building scalable applications across diverse domains. Enthusiastic about turning unknowns into efficient solutions. Currently pursuing a career in AI through contributing to impactful projects in the field. I spend my free time on analog photography and music.

bullets: Brought a prototype clarifier to life for the chemistry lab of a beet sugar factory. I wrote the software that keeps its chemical solutions at exactly the right concentration and temperature, building both the back-end logic and the front-end interface on a Raspberry Pi. End to end and by myself.
Personal web-interface to analyse stock prices for the personal use.
One of the lead engineers behind the track-and-trace software that keeps tobacco production compliant with the traceability requirements of the EU Tobacco Products Directive.

Developing, deploying and maintaining software across the whole chain: data applications that aggregate and process production data, control logic for industrial machines, HMI design and vision system configuration.

Led several projects that reshaped our software architecture and brought AI into the company in a secure, safety-compliant way. Highlights include successful design and delivery of several prototype machines, propsal and adaptation of a modular approach to our software through a shared in-house library. Recently led the adaptation of Claude Code within the software department, from the initial research and infrastructure setup to defining the Markdown-based skills and routines we now use every day.
Staying close to clients throughout a machine's life, supporting them remotely during development and service, and on the factory floor during commissioning.
Working daily with engineers from other departments and with product managers to turn requirements into working systems.
Conducted research as part of a project entitled “Autonomous Detection and Classification of Bituminous Joints in Highway Pavement Using Two-Staged and Residual-Based Convolutional Autoencoder.

Extracted and preprocessed intensity-based data from a laser-triangulation system and developed an end-to-end unsupervised pipeline for bituminous joint detection. My work addressed the following research areas: label sparsity, anomaly detection, feature space inhomogeneity and normalization challenges.
Thesis outcomes received high acclaim, earning a grade of 7.5 from academia and recognition from the host company, where the proposed approach established a benchmark for future projects.
